title: Establish the pinned workspace, contracts and verification infrastructure
description: WHY: One reproducible bootstrap and published contracts must precede independent worker implementation. SCOPE: workspace, pinned upstream, native Solid 2 contracts, executable test harness, traceable source/test inventory and parallel execution protocol. Read docs/architecture.md, docs/solid2-contract.md and docs/parallel-execution.md. Bootstrap is the first implementation ticket; harness and upstream/docs/distribution tracks then proceed independently. Component work follows concrete foundation prerequisites, not this epic. NON-GOALS: migrating the old Solid port or implementing components during scaffolding. DONE WHEN: children provide runnable commands and stable write boundaries, source baseline is immutable, and every later task can execute without inventing infrastructure.
acceptance: Bootstrap, harness and mapping infrastructure have passing proof checks.
One explicit owner controls shared manifests and contracts.
No reference repository is modified.

title: Bootstrap workspace, pinned upstream submodule and Solid 2 structural contracts
description: WHY: All implementers need one compatible toolchain and shared contracts. READ FIRST: project architecture/Solid2/parallel docs, sourcePaths at React SHA 19511bb171f3b360b006c94cf6d07e53cb446505, and all foundation ticket interfaces. IMPLEMENT: initialize a minimal pnpm workspace with private root and private packages/solid placeholder; do not overwrite existing Beads/planning files. Add independent upstream/base-ui Git submodule tracking master at the pinned SHA, leaving ../ref untouched. Record verifiedParitySha=null. Pin solid-js/@solidjs/web/compiler/babel-plugin to 2.0.0-rc.13, vite-plugin 3.0.0-next.47 and testing-library 1.0.0-beta.3; verify/pin Vite8, TypeScript, Vitest, jsdom, user-event, DOM Testing Library, Node and pnpm compatible engines rather than adopting unrelated upstream engine versions. Use @solidjs/web JSX ownership. Publish type-only structural interfaces for live render props/state, native events/refs, controlled requests, raw element access, transition status, item metadata, popup handle attachment, field registration and floating tree. Required and optional context policy must be explicit. Use upstream shapes but remove React types; avoid concrete public-component imports in contracts. Framework-native render callbacks and class spelling are intentional adaptations; preserve externally meaningful Base UI names through explicit aliases. Implement only a small compile/render/SSR proof fixture, not production components. Establish exact command names in docs/contracts.md: typescript, test:jsdom <filter> --no-watch, test:ssr, test:types, test:contracts, test:coverage-map, build:package and later test:browsers/test:parity. Accept --no-watch consistently by normalization if runner syntax differs. WRITE BOUNDARY: listed files; hand manifest/lock ownership to bsolid-dist-contract when this ticket closes. NON-GOALS: docs framework implementation, full build pipeline or component stubs pretending parity. VALIDATE: frozen install, JSX typecheck, client/server compiler smoke, runtime version identity and unmodified source SHA/status. Record commands and versions.
acceptance: Clean frozen install and client/server JSX proof pass with one pinned Solid 2 runtime.
Submodule and tracking record match the baseline; verified parity is null.
Shared structural interfaces and command contract are published without React types.
No package publication or reference mutation occurs.
Foundation workers have explicit importable contracts and disjoint implementation ownership.

title: Build Solid-native jsdom, type and SSR harness with source conformance adapters
description: WHY: Every parallel component worker needs the same executable behavior oracle and cleanup rules. READ FIRST: sourcePaths plus Solid2 testing/reactivity/rendering docs and bootstrap command contract. IMPLEMENT: Vitest jsdom/browser-development resolution, separate Node/server build project, strict declaration fixtures and @solidjs/testing-library next render(() => JSX). Own createRenderer, native event/user interactions, cleanup, conformance and popup conformance adapters. Preserve accessible-role/attribute/state/callback assertions while replacing React act/rerender mechanics with reactive prop hosts and explicit Solid flush at synchronous observation boundaries. Support props changing on the same mounted node. Capture native event currentTarget and custom pointer timestamps; timer helpers distinguish microtasks, RAF and animation completion. Fail unexpected runtime warnings and owner leaks, with narrowly named tests for expected diagnostics. SSR fixture compiles separately and proves hydration IDs without sharing client runtime modules. Keep browser-only cases discoverable but do not run full browser qualification now. Publish complete test command examples and a source-case annotation format; do not turn jsdom limitations into blanket skips. Conformance tests cover live class/style/state, render callback composition, ref disposal, external event prevention and DOM node identity. WRITE BOUNDARY: harness/config only; dependencies/scripts through manifest integrator. NON-GOALS: component implementations, replacing source assertions with snapshots, or claiming browser parity. VALIDATE: positive fixture, deliberately broken reactive-prop fixture, cleanup failure fixture, wrong-server-condition fixture, type-error fixture and SSR fixture each produce the expected result. No unfinished root barrel is required for family-local tests.
acceptance: Documented family test/type/SSR commands run against independent fixtures.
Conformance assertions detect lost prop reactivity, event ordering and DOM identity regressions.
Every render is disposed; unexpected diagnostics fail tests.
Server/client conditions and compiler targets are independently verified.
Browser scenarios remain inventoried for final execution.

title: Generate exhaustive source, exports and test-scenario ownership manifests
description: WHY: A component checklist alone misses new exports, helpers and shared test scenarios. READ FIRST: canonical exports, source trees, test generation helpers and ticket ownership metadata. IMPLEMENT: enumerate every tracked runtime/type/test/docs/build input from the pinned Git tree, not node_modules or a dirty working tree. Record source path/blob hash, target paths, owner ticket, disposition (translated/pure-adapted/framework-only/excluded-with-reason), transitive consumers and baseline. Export keys include internals, temporal adapters, types and unstable-use-media-query. Inventory test/spec paths and runtime-expanded test names/parameters/conformance scenarios when the upstream harness can collect them; static parsing alone must flag unresolved dynamic cases rather than assert full coverage. Use a separate throwaway upstream verification checkout for running original tests, never alter the canonical submodule or ../ref. Define per-family/foundation ledger schema supporting pending-browser, blocked, passing, adapted and upstream-skipped cases. Aggregate without writing worker-owned files. Detect missing/duplicate ownership and unaccounted additions/deletions. Validate mapping relative paths and reasoned React-only exclusions; unknown source paths fail. WRITE BOUNDARY: central schema/generator/reports, not component ledgers. NON-GOALS: automatically translating behavior, counting test files as test-case parity, or silently skipping a dependency installation failure. VALIDATE: fixture adds/renames/deletes exports and parameterized tests; demonstrate missing mappings fail, overrides retain provenance, and deterministic generation reads exact SHA. Report any upstream execution blockers explicitly.
acceptance: Every package export and tracked runtime/test family has an owner or explicit disposition.
Parameterized/conformance tests are expanded or explicitly unresolved.
Mapping drift, rename/deletion and missing-owner fixtures fail correctly.
Generators do not overwrite component/foundation ledgers or reference files.

title: Make weekly upstream reconciliation reproducible and resumable
description: WHY: Fetching React commits must translate into explicit Solid work rather than silent drift. IN SCOPE: read-only pinned Git submodule, candidate versus verified baseline, change classification, reverse dependency impact, Beads update episodes, completion evidence and resume/recovery. Read docs/upstream-workflow.md. Child scripts operate on exact immutable from/to SHAs. NON-GOALS: auto-committing, resetting developer work, auto-advancing parity, or auto-publishing. DONE WHEN: one command creates an auditable update episode, independent owners can reconcile in parallel, and the verified SHA moves only after all required evidence passes.
acceptance: Weekly update workflow handles initial/null baseline and subsequent verified updates.
Repeated/resumed runs do not lose or duplicate work.
No unknown change is silently classified as irrelevant.

title: Implement init/update/status wrappers around the pinned upstream submodule
description: WHY: The user needs a friction-free fetch command without changing React source or losing a reconciliation baseline. READ FIRST: docs/upstream-workflow.md and bootstrap's .gitmodules/tracking/upstream.json. IMPLEMENT: pnpm upstream:init/update/status wrappers. Init checks out the recorded SHA; update fetches origin master, resolves immutable candidate SHA, checks ancestry and generates a from/to record. Keep baseline source, candidate and verifiedParitySha separate; verified parity begins null. Reject dirty submodule or wrong URL/branch, missing recorded commit and non-fast-forward history with actionable output. Never reset or stash automatically. Store immutable episodes under tracking/updates/<from>-<to>/, serialize state writes and protect concurrent calls with an explicit lock. While a candidate is active, queue a fetched SHA without moving the checkout under workers. Same-SHA invocation is a no-op and repeated interrupted invocation resumes. Preserve the prior verified pin and support explicit abandonment that retains historical reports. Shared package scripts are integrated by manifest owner. WRITE BOUNDARY: CLI/git adapter/test/schema; runtime generated records are owned by the active episode coordinator. NON-GOALS: merge React into Solid, patch upstream, commit gitlinks or infer reconciliation completion. VALIDATE: local bare fixture remotes cover first clone, unchanged HEAD, normal update, dirty worktree, remote error, rewritten history, missing submodule, concurrent calls and interrupted state writes. Use RTK on all terminal invocations and preserve machine-readable output for parsing.
acceptance: Documented one-command fetch works on a fresh clone and existing checkout.
Candidate never overwrites the verified SHA or an active worker checkout.
Dirty/reference paths remain untouched across all failure fixtures.
Repeat/resume/concurrency behavior is deterministic.

title: Map weekly source changes into idempotent parallel Beads reconciliation tickets
description: WHY: Every relevant upstream change needs an executable owner ticket, not a commit-summary dump. READ FIRST: source mappings/coverage schema and weekly state contract. IMPLEMENT: use exact Git from/to diff with rename detection, changed blobs and commit context. Classify component runtime, shared utilities, public types/exports, tests, styling attributes/CSS variables, docs/demos, dependency/build and license changes. Compute reverse dependencies from source imports plus explicit dynamic/semantic edges. Produce an immutable change report with unknown entries requiring triage. Create one Beads epic per range and owner-scoped tasks with exact changed lines/files, mapped target files, test cases, acceptance, dependencies and write allowlist; shared changes precede only affected consumers. New components/exports generate implementation tickets. Rename/delete changes demand explicit removal/alias decisions and tests. React-only no-op requires a recorded rationale. Deduplicate by episode+owner+change fingerprint; handle changed reports explicitly rather than overwriting manually edited tickets. WRITE BOUNDARY: impact/Beads adapter and template; no implementation changes. NON-GOALS: automated semantic code translation or blanket marking tests covered because their file did not change. VALIDATE: fixtures for event utility impacting many families, docs-only change, added export, deleted helper, renamed test, overlapping episodes and restart after partial ticket creation. Assert dependency acyclicity and no concurrent ownership collision.
acceptance: Every diff entry is mapped or visibly untriaged.
Tickets contain source/target/test details and real prerequisite edges.
Repeated or partially failed generation creates no duplicate episode tasks.
Shared changes identify transitive consumers while unrelated owners remain parallelizable.

title: Gate parity advancement and rehearse a complete weekly update
description: WHY: Fetch completion is not behavioral parity. READ FIRST: weekly state/mapping schemas and all qualification gates. IMPLEMENT: upstream:verify checks immutable episode SHAs, source cleanliness, complete change dispositions, task closure, target source/test mappings and required evidence hashes. Require impact-selected unit/type/integration/docs/package checks, plus appropriate browser regression evidence after the initial browser qualification exists. Advance verifiedParitySha atomically only for the exact tested candidate with no unresolved blockers. A historical partial component baseline must never be called global parity. Record toolchain/command/artifact versions and retained previous verified state. Rehearse from two real immutable upstream commits in isolated fixture worktrees; can select an older small range for reproducibility without downgrading project source. Exercise discovery, tickets, changed-component handoff, verification failure, interruption/resume and successful advancement. No code auto-commits or publications. WRITE BOUNDARY: verifier/tests/runbook/rehearsal; worker outputs remain read-only. NON-GOALS: bypassing a failed source test as framework difference without documented review. VALIDATE: dirty SHA, missing evidence, open task, unknown path, stale report and failed browser checks all block advancement; successful exact evidence permits one idempotent advance.
acceptance: Parity SHA cannot advance with an open task, mapping gap or stale/failed evidence.
A reproducible rehearsal covers resume and recovery without modifying refs.
Runbook gives one-command fetch, agent dispatch, verify and recovery steps.
Initial global parity additionally requires final qualification.

title: Integrate all families and qualify release parity against React
description: WHY: Independent task success must be joined into a complete tested library. IN SCOPE: root exports, all-source coverage, real cross-family integration, original React baseline, final browser/SSR/accessibility evidence and release-readiness decision. Component implementation gates are distinct from final browser-qualified parity. Read project architecture and parallel rules. Each test lane owns separate fixtures/reports and files; failures return to their code owner via concrete follow-up tickets. NON-GOALS: rewriting shared code in test tickets, publishing without instruction or claiming zero bugs. DONE WHEN: source/export coverage is complete and all stated release checks pass at one pinned upstream/runtime/artifact tuple.
acceptance: All export/source cases accounted for.
Cross-family and final browser/SSR/accessibility evidence passes.
Release-readiness evidence names exact tested versions and unresolved scope.

title: Wire complete exports and replay real cross-family non-browser scenarios
description: WHY: Source-local worker tests may have used contract fixtures before sibling families existed. READ FIRST: every completed worker ledger, source export map, index.test.tsx and cross-family source suites. IMPLEMENT: connect all root/type exports and intentional internal aliases; submit manifest key/target updates to distribution owner, never edit its manifest concurrently. Compare exports/namespace parts/generic types to the pinned source with documented framework adaptations. Replay contract cases with real components: Toolbar+ToggleGroup+Toggle, Field/Form controls in portals, CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup validation, nested Dialog/Menu/Select/Combobox, tooltip triggers using custom render, CSP styles and RTL. Preserve source scenarios; do not replace asserted semantics with snapshots. Identify unowned pure internals/build inputs and explicitly assign missing work before closure. Prevent React runtime/type leaks and legacy Solid imports through an import-graph check. Centralize shared aliases while family barrels remain owned by their family workers. WRITE BOUNDARY: aggregate exports/types/integration tests/report only; code fixes go to responsible workers. NON-GOALS: treating contract fixtures as final parity, executing final browser suite here, or silently expanding public API. VALIDATE: complete jsdom, strict types, source-map audit and SSR smoke using runnable harness commands; no unresolved non-browser source scenarios. Record deferred layout/browser cases with exact final-lane owners.
acceptance: All upstream export keys and namespace capabilities are wired or explicitly adapted.
Real cross-family non-browser tests replace provisional contract-only evidence.
No unmapped implementation/test source remains.
Runtime/declaration graphs contain no React or Solid1 dependencies.
All browser-only obligations have final-lane owners.

title: Certify initial component implementation and non-browser coverage completeness
description: WHY: Downstream docs and distribution need a clear implementation-complete gate without confusing it with final browser-qualified release parity. READ FIRST: all component/foundation/integration ledgers and source inventory. IMPLEMENT: verify every family and exported utility/internal capability is present; all source test scenarios have a target test or reviewed framework-only disposition; all non-browser tests/typechecks pass; deferred browser cases are authored, countable and assigned to final qualification. Validate that test results match the exact code/toolchain/SHA and no worker left placeholder exports, TODO assertions or disabled failures. Publish an immutable gate report with counts, versions, commands and evidence paths. Any new non-browser failure creates a concrete blocker ticket and leaves this gate open. WRITE BOUNDARY: gate record only. NON-GOALS: changing code, accepting missing features as exclusions, setting verifiedParitySha, publishing or claiming browser verification. VALIDATE: source-map audit, all worker states, aggregate suite and strict types. The report must explicitly say browser qualification pending until later gates pass.
acceptance: Zero unassigned exports or non-browser scenarios.
Complete aggregate jsdom/type suite passes.
Browser cases are retained and assigned, never counted as passing.
No upstream verified parity advancement at this gate.

title: Run final cross-browser interaction and React-versus-Solid parity qualification
description: WHY: jsdom cannot establish layout, real focus, pointer capture or browser gesture parity. This is the final browser phase requested by the user. READ FIRST: all pending-browser ledgers, pinned React runner and pointer helpers. IMPLEMENT: independent React and Solid hosts under one scenario protocol; run original React tests in an isolated exact-SHA verification checkout, not the read-only canonical source. Use Chromium/Firefox/WebKit as upstream scenario requirements permit. Replay keyboard, touch/pen/mouse, hover intent, nested Escape/outside press, focus guards/return, scroll lock, portals/shadow/iframe, collisions/arrows, slider geometry, NumberField scrubbing, Drawer snap/virtual keyboard, ScrollArea drag and animations/interrupted close. Compare observable DOM/ARIA, callback reasons/order/cancellation and form payloads; normalize only documented generated IDs and framework markers, never behavioral differences. Preserve event timestamps in gesture tests. No arbitrary sleeps or snapshot-only assertions. Record upstream failures separately with reproduction; they are not a Solid pass. WRITE BOUNDARY: qualification runners/fixtures/reports only; source corrections become owner tickets. NON-GOALS: component redesign or weakening tests to force agreement. VALIDATE: all retained browser cases resolve to evidence; failures keep this gate open; store exact browser/build/toolchain/SHA and reproducible commands.
acceptance: All queued browser scenarios execute in appropriate real browsers.
React/Solid observable parity holds with only documented normalizations.
No unresolved port-caused failures or missing cases.
Reference repositories remain unmodified.

title: Qualify streaming SSR, hydration, root events and disposal under production builds
description: WHY: Correct client-only rendering can hide hydration ID drift, request leaks and incorrect compiled server exports. READ FIRST: RC13 rendering/SSR/Portal docs, exact declarations and source hydration/prehydration suites. IMPLEMENT: production and development server/client builds for initially open/closed controls, keepMounted, conditional children, multiple render roots/renderIds, streaming Loading/Errored boundaries, async list updates and concurrent requests. Verify stable IDs/label ownership, portal post-hydration client-only semantics and custom ShadowRoot/iframe containers. Prove root-scoped events work once across nested roots/portals and disappear on disposal. Ensure imported package server paths never read browser globals. Test CSP nonce propagation/disabled style elements and source-specific prehydration behavior in Tabs/Slider; no suppressHydrationWarning equivalent used to hide incorrect structures. Repeated mount/unmount and async result-after-disposal checks detect leaked observers/listeners/timers/owners; record counts where deterministic rather than relying only on heap screenshots. WRITE BOUNDARY: independent fixtures/report, not shared harness/build/component files. NON-GOALS: a new metaframework/router or default async suspension for internal measurement. VALIDATE: no unapproved hydration/dev warnings, initial markup semantics and post-hydration interaction match source, all root/request isolation cases pass on built artifacts.
acceptance: Concurrent SSR requests and multiple roots do not share mutable state or IDs.
Streaming/hydration fixtures attach without unexplained warnings or event loss.
Portals, CSP and prehydration behavior match documented contracts.
Disposal releases owned resources and ignores stale async completions.

title: Qualify accessibility, keyboard operation and platform-sensitive behavior
description: WHY: Accessibility is a behavioral contract beyond role snapshots and automated rule checks. READ FIRST: upstream accessibility guidance, screen-reader command in package.json and family keyboard/ARIA suites. IMPLEMENT: independent scenario matrix for every family covering accessible names/descriptions, required/invalid announcements, disabled/readOnly behavior, keyboard-only operation, RTL, reduced motion, forced colors and zoom. Exercise nested modal escape/focus restore, composite active descendants and dynamic item removal, Toast live regions, touch-trigger default focus and form error focus. Run automated accessibility assertions on representative composed states, plus manual/assistive-technology scripts for announcements that automation cannot prove. Reuse upstream screen-reader setup where compatible without importing React harness internals; document exact platform/AT/browser combinations. Unsupported local automation leaves a specific open execution blocker, not an invented pass or copied upstream claim. WRITE BOUNDARY: accessibility fixtures/report/protocol only; no edits to component code or docs family fragments. NON-GOALS: claiming universal accessibility from axe alone or translating unrelated private upstream demos. VALIDATE: each matrix row has pass evidence or unresolved blocker; replay repaired regressions; report concrete support claims to documentation owners. This runs in parallel with browser and hydration qualification after components complete.
acceptance: All families have keyboard/ARIA coverage with real composed-state evidence.
RTL, disabled, reduced-motion and nested focus cases pass.
Screen-reader claims match recorded platform-specific checks.
No unresolved accessibility regressions at release readiness.

title: Join final evidence and certify the exact initial upstream parity baseline
description: WHY: Publishing requires one coherent evidence tuple, not unrelated green runs. READ FIRST: all gate reports, packed archive checksum, complete docs report and upstream rehearsal. IMPLEMENT: require closed non-browser, browser, hydration, accessibility, docs, distribution and maintenance checks for the same source/runtime/library revision. Verify no open parity bugs or hidden test exclusions and reconcile every public/internal export. Record final component/test counts, browser versions, API adaptations, license notices, artifact checksum and release prerequisites. Only now authorize the upstream verifier's initial verifiedParitySha advancement to the pinned source; this ticket itself does not publish, commit or push. If npm identity changes after this gate, invalidate affected package/docs evidence and rerun before publication. WRITE BOUNDARY: final gate record only. NON-GOALS: a guarantee of zero future bugs, publishing under an assumed npm scope or ignoring pending platform checks. VALIDATE: cross-report revision/hash checks and full blocker-state audit; absent/stale evidence fails. Distribution publication must depend on this ticket in addition to its package checks.
acceptance: All required final evidence refers to one exact source/runtime/artifact tuple.
Zero unresolved parity blockers and all exports/scenarios accounted for.
Initial verified upstream baseline advances only after this gate.
Publishing remains separately authorized and dependency-gated.
